Patient.template: Using only the retrieved PostgreSQL schema metadata, find the relation or joins that represent a patient in any of these source schemas: {source_schemas}. Generate one SELECT filtered to patient key {patient_key}. Return exactly one row and these aliases: patient key AS _patient_key, administrative gender AS _gender, death date/time AS _death_datetime. Use NULL only for unavailable optional values. Do not assume any table or column name. Fully qualify every relation.

Encounter.template: Using only the retrieved PostgreSQL schema metadata, find the broadest canonical relation that represents patient encounters, visits, or admissions in any of these source schemas: {source_schemas}. It must include general encounters regardless of whether dependent clinical events, procedures, measurements, locations, sessions, or subordinate stays exist. Prefer one relation that directly stores the patient key, encounter key, and period. Do not use INNER/CROSS JOIN, EXISTS, or IN-subquery against a dependent relation to establish encounter existence or narrow the cohort. Do not choose a subordinate episode when a documented parent encounter/visit relation is available. Generate a SELECT filtered only to patient key {patient_key}{encounter_override_clause}. Return one unique row per canonical encounter with: patient key AS _patient_key, encounter/visit key AS _encounter_key, a documented source encounter/admission type column AS _encounter_type, start date/time AS _start_datetime, end date/time AS _end_datetime. Every output expression MUST be a documented source column or NULL. A quoted label is forbidden. Order by start date/time descending nulls last and limit {limit}. Do not assume any table or column name. Fully qualify every relation.
